title: Service Advisor
description:
Service Advisor

Cheltenham £28,000 Basic Salary £33,000 OTE

Good Service Advisors make a busy workshop feel effortless.

We're looking for an experienced Service Advisor to join an established automotive dealership in Cheltenham.

You'll be at the centre of the customer journey, working closely with the workshop to keep vehicles moving, customers informed and expectations managed from the moment a vehicle is booked in through to collection.

If you know your way around a busy aftersales department, enjoy working with people and take pride in getting the details right, we'd like to talk.

The opportunity

This is a customer-facing role with plenty of variety. You'll be managing several vehicles and customer conversations throughout the day, balancing customer expectations with workshop capacity and making sure everyone knows what's happening.

You'll be responsible for:
- Booking vehicles into the workshop and understanding exactly what the customer needs
- Preparing accurate job cards and making sure the right information is captured from the outset
- Liaising closely with Technicians, Workshop Controllers and the wider aftersales team
- Providing clear estimates and explaining recommended work in a way customers can understand
- Keeping customers updated throughout the repair and servicing process
- Discussing additional work and obtaining customer authorisation where required
- Explaining technical information without unnecessary jargon
- Advising customers on servicing, maintenance and future requirements
- Managing queries and resolving issues calmly and professionally
- Making sure vehicles are ready for collection and the handover is smooth
- Building strong customer relationships that encourage customers to return
- Working towards customer satisfaction, departmental and commercial KPIs
- Following dealership and manufacturer processes accurately

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone who understands that great Service Advising is about more than booking cars in and handing over keys.

You'll need to be confident with customers, commercially aware and organised enough to keep control when the workshop gets busy.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience as a Service Advisor within an automotive dealership
- A good understanding of workshop and aftersales operations
- Excellent communication skills, both face-to-face and over the phone
- Confidence discussing recommended and additional work with customers
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- The ability to manage competing priorities without losing sight of the customer
- A proactive approach to problem solving
- A positive, professional and team-focused attitude
- A full UK driving licence

Franchised dealership experience would be advantageous, but it isn't everything. If you have strong automotive customer service experience and the right approach, we're happy to have a conversation.

What's on offer
- £28,000 basic salary
- £33,000 OTE
- Established automotive dealership
- Supportive aftersales environment
- Training and development opportunities
- Long-term career progression
- The opportunity to build on your automotive experience within an established team

Let's talk

If you're an experienced Service Advisor in or around Cheltenham and you're open to hearing about something new, we'd like to hear from you.

You don't have to be actively looking.

If you're curious about the role, we'll give you the full picture, answer your questions honestly and let you decide whether it's right for you.

No pressure. No hard sell. Just a straightforward conversation about the opportunity and what you're looking for next.

Apply today or let us know you are interested for a confidential conversation with Pembrook Resourcing.

Please note: dealership details will be discussed confidentially with suitable candidates during the recruitment process.

title: 2 x Credit Controllers (contract to perm)
description:
- Credit Controller x 2
- Gloucester
- £30,000
- Hybrid (4 days in the office during initial 2-3 weeks of training, reduced to 3 days thereafter)
- 6 month contract initially, with strong possibility of a permanent role

A leading UK facilities services company based in Gloucester is currently looking for at least two experienced Credit Controllers to join its order to cash team as soon as possible on an initial 6 month contract. There is a strong possibility of the roles turning into permanent opportunities should the successful candidates prove themselves. You will be tasked with an initial project of clearing a backlog of over £3 million in outstanding UK B2 B debt, dealing with high volumes of accounts.
- Manage an allocated portfolio of customer accounts and ensure outstanding balances are actively monitored.
- Make a high volume of outbound calls to customers each day to chase outstanding invoices and overdue balances.
- Maintain a structured call schedule, prioritising accounts by value, age of debt, and risk profile.
- Engage professionally and confidently with accounts payable contacts, finance teams, and decision-makers.
- Follow up all calls with written confirmation of agreed payment dates and any dispute resolutions.
- Assist with bad debt identification.
- Identify and investigate unallocated or short payments, liaising with customers and internal teams to resolve discrepancies.
- Maintain up-to-date and accurate records of all payment activity within the collections system.
- Refer unresolved disputes to the query management team with supporting documentation, customer correspondence, invoice details, and call notes.
- Maintain regular communication with the query management team to monitor the progress and expected resolution date of open queries.

Experience required:
- Demonstrable experience of making high-volume outbound calls in a business-to-business (B2 B) environment.
- Previous experience within a credit control, accounts receivable or sales ledger environment
- Strong numerical ability with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident, clear, and professional telephone manner.
- Ability to handle difficult conversations calmly and assertively while maintaining customer relationships.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience using a finance or ERP system (e.g. Sage, SAP, Xero, or similar).
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills with the ability to manage a busy workload independently.
- Experience working to KPIs such as DSO targets, call volumes, or cash collection targets.
- Available on short notice

title: Office Administrator
description:
Estate Agent Office Administrator - Student & Residential Lettings

Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am - 5:00pm
Pay: £12.71 - £13.00 per hour
Contract: Temporary to Permanent
Pay increase upon successful completion of the temporary-to-permanent period

Are you organised, approachable and proactive, and looking for a varied role where no two days are quite the same?

Due to an exciting increase in our property portfolio across both student accommodation and residential lettings, we are looking for an enthusiastic Office Administrator to join a busy and growing estate and lettings team.

This is much more than a traditional administration position. You'll be involved throughout the lettings journey - from advertising properties and arranging viewings to supporting new tenants with their move-in and ensuring all the necessary paperwork, council and utility arrangements are completed.

You'll communicate with a wide range of people every day, including students, private tenants, landlords, social housing contacts, local councils, contractors and utility providers, making this an interesting and people-focused role.

The Role

Working at the heart of the lettings office, you'll help ensure the property portfolio is efficiently managed and prospective and existing tenants receive a professional and friendly service.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Creating, uploading and managing property advertisements on OpenRent and other relevant platforms
- Ensuring property listings are accurate, attractive and kept up to date
- Responding to enquiries from prospective tenants and providing information about available properties
- Managing and coordinating the property viewing diary, ensuring appointments are organised efficiently for Louisa
- Booking, confirming and rearranging property viewings with prospective tenants
- Following up on enquiries and helping move prospective tenants through the lettings process
- Preparing tenancy documentation and completing the administration required when a new tenant is secured
- Coordinating tenant move-ins and ensuring all necessary documentation is completed
- Liaising with local councils regarding council tax and other tenancy-related matters
- Communicating with gas, electricity, water and other utility providers when tenants move in or out
- Engaging with students, private tenants and individuals within social housing
- Maintaining accurate tenant, landlord and property records
- Supporting tenancy renewals, move-ins and move-outs
- Liaising with landlords, contractors and tenants regarding property matters and maintenance requirements
- Helping coordinate maintenance enquiries and ensuring issues are directed to the appropriate person
- Providing ongoing administrative and customer service support to tenants throughout their tenancy
- Managing telephone calls, emails, filing, data entry and general office correspondence
- Supporting the wider team with additional duties as the property portfolio continues to expand

About You

We're looking for someone who is friendly, confident, organised and comfortable dealing with a wide variety of people.

You'll need to be able to manage several priorities at once, whether that's arranging a last-minute viewing, responding to a tenant enquiry, updating a property advert or making sure the paperwork for a new tenancy is ready.

Previous experience within administration, lettings, property, housing or customer service would be beneficial, although a positive attitude, strong communication skills and a willingness to learn are equally important.

You should be comfortable using computers and online systems, have good written and verbal communication skills and be confident speaking with tenants, landlords and external organisations.

Why Join?

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking for a position that combines administration, property, customer service and coordination.

With the portfolio expanding across both student and residential lettings, you'll have the opportunity to develop a broad understanding of the property and lettings sector while becoming an important part of a busy team.

Monday to Friday, 9:00am - 5:00pm

£12.71 - £13.00 per hour, with an increase in pay following successful completion of the temporary-to-permanent period.

If you're organised, personable and enjoy being kept busy, this could be the perfect opportunity to develop your career within a growing property business.

Apply today to find out more.

title: Finance Officer/Credit Controller
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company

Hays Accountancy & Finance are exclusively partnering with an established & prestigious educational organisation to recruit a dynamic & hands-on Finance Officer/Credit controller to join their team in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire. Reporting directly to the Billing & Collections Manager, you will be responsible for the day-to-day management of fees and income, ensuring billing is accurate, along with credit control processes to ensure overdue accounts are monitored and followed up professionally. This is an exciting and varied opportunity for a Finance Officer/Credit Controller to join the organisation through a period of process improvement and change, where you can really add value and make the role your own. Best suited to finance professionals with previous Credit Control experience, who enjoy relationship building both internally & externally.

Your new role

Your key duties will involve credit control processes, including monitoring outstanding fees, managing payment plans and escalating any issues to senior management, along with assisting with debt reporting. You will prepare and issue termly fee bills, reconcile billing accounts, maintain accurate customer records, reconcile payments, resolve accounts queries directly with the customers, along with supporting process improvement projects for the billing/income processes. You will prepare and process direct debit collections, administer direct debit processes in compliance with BACs regulations, and investigate any failed collections. You will support maintaining the fees billing system, working closely with other teams around the organisation to ensure accurate data input. This is an evolving and changing position where you can really add value working within a close-knit team, reporting directly to the Billing & Collections Manager.

What you'll need to succeed

To be considered for this permanent Finance Officer/Credit Control role, you will need some experience in a similar position, a team player who is comfortable working within a close-knit team. A strong problem solver capable of using their own initiative, experience of accurate data management for invoicing and proven experience of debtor management. The ability to work under pressure to meet deadlines with high accuracy, excellent communication skills and a telephone manner to build both internal and external relationships. Experience with financial systems, adaptable to organisational needs, and a process improvement mind-set. Experience within the education sector or school finance, billing systems, business to customer collections and knowledge of direct debit collections would be advantageous but not essential.

What you'll get in return

This permanent Finance Officer/Credit Control role offers a permanent salary up to £32,000 per annum, dependable on experience based in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire. A full-time role with benefits including a contributed pension scheme, use of organisations sport facilities, free lunches, life insurance, private health care options, a Christmas shutdown and more. A great opportunity to really add value by joining one of Cheltenham's most well-known educational organisations during a period of change and transformation.

What you need to do now

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now. If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Finance & Payroll Accounts Assistant - TEMP TO PERM
description:
Finance & Payroll Accounts Assistant - TEMP TO PERM

Hours: 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Location: Bourton-on-the-Water
Salary: Up to £35,000
Working pattern: Office-based, with some flexibility around start and finish times

The Role

We are looking for an organised and detail-focused Finance & Payroll Accounts Assistant. The role combines responsibility for accurate weekly payroll preparation with finance, accounts and general administrative support.

The key focus is compiling, checking and validating employee hours before weekly payroll is processed. This is not an end-to-end payroll position; payroll processing, tax and final payroll preparation are handled by an established payroll specialist.

Key Responsibilities
- Compile and validate weekly employee hours, including variable hours, pay rates, sickness, holidays and other payroll adjustments.
- Review time-recording information and compare reports across multiple systems.
- Investigate discrepancies, missing or incorrect information and liaise with managers to resolve issues.
- Ensure payroll data is accurate, complete and correctly allocated ahead of the weekly payroll deadline.
- Support Finance with payroll reporting, reconciliations, financial records and general accounts administration.
- Handle relevant cash, petty cash and payment administration.
- Maintain accurate payroll, financial and employee records, spreadsheets and internal systems.
- Respond to payroll, finance and employee queries professionally, working collaboratively with Finance, HR and management.
- Provide general administrative support to the wider business as required.

What We're Looking For
- Previous payroll experience, with a proven understanding of payroll processes and experience collating and/or checking payroll data.
- Strong Excel skills, including confidence working with formulas, checking formula accuracy and analysing spreadsheets.
- Experience analysing data from multiple systems or reports and confidently interrogating information to identify discrepancies or errors.
- Understanding of hours worked, pay rates, gross pay, deductions, net pay, holiday, sickness and different working arrangements.
- Experience in basic finance and accounts administration, including maintaining financial records, reconciliations and cash-related queries.
- Excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy and a methodical approach.
- Comfortable working to a weekly payroll cycle and fixed deadlines while maintaining accuracy in a busy environment.
- Strong organisation and prioritisation skills, with the ability to work independently and take ownership of deadlines.
- Good communication skills and confidence liaising with employees and managers.

Working Arrangements

The position is predominantly office-based, Monday to Friday, with some flexibility around start and finish times, provided business requirements and weekly payroll deadlines are met.

The role works across Finance, HR and management, requiring effective communication and collaboration.

Benefits
- Competitive salary up to £35,000.
- 20 days' holiday plus Bank Holidays.
- Pension scheme.
- Lifestyle benefits and retail discounts.
- Employee Assistance Programme.
- Career development opportunities.
- Option to purchase additional annual leave.
- Electric vehicle salary-sacrifice scheme.
- Cycle-to-work scheme.

To Be Considered

Please email me the following information:
- How many years' payroll experience you have.
- Your level of Excel experience.
- Your location and how you would travel to Bourton-on-the-Water.
- Your salary expectations.
- Your availability to start.

description:
Part-Time Bookkeeper (16-18 Hours Per Week)

Location: Bishops Cleeve
Hours: Approximately 16-18 hours per week with flexibility on working days and hours
Salary: £18/hr

The Opportunity

We are recruiting for an experienced and organised Bookkeeper to join our client on a part-time basis. This is an excellent opportunity for someone seeking a flexible role that can fit around existing commitments while playing a key part in the day-to-day financial operations of a successful business.

The successful candidate will be responsible for managing the company's bookkeeping activities, ensuring financial records are accurate and maintained to a high standard, whilst supporting month-end and year-end processes.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing the purchase ledger and sales ledger
- Processing invoices, payments and receipts
- Bank reconciliations and general bookkeeping duties
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns
- Maintaining accurate financial records using Sage
- Supporting month-end and year-end accounting processes
- Preparing transactional accounting information for external accountants
- Assisting with financial reporting and documentation requests
- Ensuring all records remain compliant and up to date

Skills & Experience Required
- Previous experience in a bookkeeping or finance position
- Strong knowledge of purchase ledger and sales ledger processes

What's on Offer?
- Flexible working hours around 16-18 hours per week
- Opportunity to work within a friendly and supportive environment
- Varied and autonomous role
- Competitive salary based on experience
- Long-term opportunity with a growing business, including twice annual bonus

If you are an experienced Bookkeeper looking for a flexible, part-time opportunity where you can make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Salesforce Administrator
description:
Our client, a group of market-leading brands deliver engineered water solutions such as pumps, booster sets, flow meter chambers and pressurisation units to customers across the UK and beyond. Based in Gloucester, they are now looking for a Salesforce Administrator to join their team.

As Salesforce Administrator you will be responsible for the day-to-day operation, configuration and ongoing development of the Group's Salesforce platform (Sales Cloud and Marketing Cloud) across their trading entities. Sitting within Group IT and reporting to the Head of IT, the role brings Salesforce capability in-house.

Please note- this role is based in Gloucester, with occasional travel to Henley, Colchester and Redditch

Key Responsibilities

Build, Automation & Development (Primary Focus)
- Design, build, test and maintain automation using Flow (record-triggered, screen, scheduled and autolaunched), validation rules, approval processes, and assignment and escalation rules.
- Configure and make targeted change amendments; commission bespoke development externally only where genuinely warranted.
- Investigate and resolve issues. Identifying root cause rather than symptom.

Platform Administration & Configuration
- Administer and configure Salesforce Sales Cloud and Marketing Cloud environments.
- Manage users, roles, profiles, permission sets, sharing rules and data access across clouds, applying least-privilege principles.
- Maintain reports, dashboards, list views and analytics used by commercial and marketing teams.

Release, Change & Environment Management
- Operate within Group IT change control: raise, document and obtain approval for changes in line with FWG IT policy, with defined rollback plans for higher-risk work.

Support & Incident Management
- Act as the escalation point for Salesforce incidents and service requests, working within Group IT service management processes and agreed response expectations.
- Triage, prioritise and resolve user issues, with clear criteria for the small number of cases that warrant escalation to Salesforce Support or an external partner.
- Maintain a prioritised backlog of enhancements and defects, visible to IT leadership and business stakeholders.
- Produce and maintain user guidance and deliver training to improve adoption and reduce avoidable demand.

Stakeholder, Vendor & People
- Work directly with commercial and marketing stakeholders across the Group's entities to gather requirements and translate them into scalable solutions - including the ability to challenge change that would damage the platform.

Administrative / Other
- Ensure Salesforce documentation, configuration records and process maps are maintained and accessible to relevant stakeholders.
- Any other duty that may reasonably be required by the Head of IT or IT Director.

Requirements
- Proven experience as a Salesforce Administrator.
- Strong working knowledge of Sales Cloud; hands-on experience of Marketing Cloud.
- Excellent communication skills and a business-focused mindset; able to work with non-technical stakeholders and technical IT colleagues alike.
- Comfortable operating as the in-house expert, working to IT governance, change control and documentation standards.
- Hands-on experience in a Salesforce greenfield implementation.
- Marketing Cloud Email Specialist, Administrator or Consultant certification.
- Experience of Salesforce integration with Sage 200 or EFACS, or comparable ERP integration.
- Familiarity with Pardot / Account Engagement, Tableau, CPQ or Salesforce-integrated applications.
- Experience in a multi-site or multi-entity business environment.
- Experience mentoring or supporting the development of a junior administrator.

Benefits

Monday- Friday 8am-5pm
Salary - £32,000

title: Administrative Assistant
description:
Location: Cheltenham, Gloucestershire
Contract: Temporary, 2 to 3 months
Hours: Part-time, 21 hours over 3 days per week
Pay: £14.34 per hour (+ £1.73 holiday pay)
Start Date: ASAP

Prospectus is delighted to be supporting a leading national children's charity in the search for a temporary Administrative Assistant to join their Youth Support Service. Please note that due to the access to vulnerable young people and their data, this role is subject to a basic DBS check and five years' reference checks. This is a fully on-site position based at Whaddon Youth Hub.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and proactive administrator to support a busy frontline service that works with young people, families and partner organisations across the local community. The successful candidate will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the service, providing high-quality administrative support and acting as a welcoming first point of contact for visitors and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities:
- Provide efficient and effective administrative support to Service Managers, Youth Workers and external partners.
- Act as the first point of contact at the Youth Hub, delivering a welcoming, professional and supportive experience.
- Manage incoming telephone, email and in-person enquiries.
- Coordinate meetings, diaries and service administration activities.
- Maintain accurate records, databases and electronic filing systems.
- Support the preparation and distribution of reports, meeting papers and correspondence.
- Assist with monitoring expenditure, processing invoices and financial administration.
- Order and manage office supplies and support the smooth operation of the hub.
- Ensure confidentiality and compliance when handling sensitive information.
- Provide general administrative support across the wider Youth Support Service.

Key Requirements:
- Recent, relevant experience in an administrative or office management position, ideally within a charitable or not-for-profit organisation, with knowledge of youth, family, or care services.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with confidence dealing with a wide range of different audiences and stakeholders, including the public.
- Proactive and adaptable approach with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Strong attention to detail and a completer-finisher mindset.
- Advanced IT skills including Outlook, Word and Excel, with experience using databases and reporting systems.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately, with consideration of data privacy.

CVs will be reviewed on a rolling basis so if you're interested, please apply ASAP with your CV in Word format.

At Prospectus, we believe recruitment should be human-led and we are committed to supporting you throughout your application journey. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on age, gender, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, marital status, or pregnancy/maternity. While AI may be used to support our administrative process, all applications are reviewed by people and all hiring decisions are made by experienced recruiters.
